- g_dwStateInitPending also accessed by: GetGlobalState, ReadDemoRecordFileInternal

0x6FB6C990.name: ProcessMessageLogRecords
0x6FB6C990.comment:
Process pending message log records from the global log buffer chain.

Algorithm:
1. Validate global logging state (g_dwGlobalFlag and g_pCurrentLogBuffer)
2. Get current game frame counter and compare against log threshold (0x6fbec31c)
3. Check if current buffer has unprocessed records (0x1f44 vs 0x1f40)
4. For each unprocessed record in 16-byte MessageLogEntry format:
   a. Validate record frame matches current frame (corruption detection)
   b. Extract record parameters from offsets +4, +8, +12
   c. Call Ordinal_10027 to prepare record for processing
   d. Call Ordinal_412 to execute the actual record processing
   e. Increment processed record count (0x1f44)
   f. Check if buffer is exhausted or chain continues (0x1f48)
5. Handle buffer chain traversal when current buffer reaches 500 record limit
6. Terminate processing when frame threshold exceeded or null buffer reached

Parameters:
No input parameters - operates on global log buffer state

Returns:
void - Processing continues until buffer exhausted or frame limit reached

Special Cases:
Frame limit exceeded (dwCurrentFrame >= 0x6fbec31c): Sets g_dwGlobalFlag = 0 to disable logging
Buffer corruption detected: Calls error handler with code 0x12a then terminates (0xffffffff)
Record overflow (>499 records): Calls error handler with code 0x189 then terminates (0xffffffff)
Buffer chain exhaustion: Returns normally when g_pCurrentLogBuffer becomes null

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1f44 (8004): Offset to current record read index in log buffer
0x1f48 (8008): Offset to next buffer pointer in chain structure  
0x1f40 (8000): Offset to total record count in current buffer
0x10 (16): Size of each MessageLogEntry record structure
0x1f4 (500): Maximum records per buffer before chain advancement
0x189 (393): Error code for record count overflow
0x12a (298): Error code for frame validation failure
0x6fbec31c: Global frame threshold for log processing cutoff
0x6fbee280: Address of g_dwGlobalFlag control variable
0x6fbaffe0: Address of g_pCurrentLogBuffer pointer

Structure Layout:
MessageLogEntry (16 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | dwFrame    | uint | Game frame when record was created
0x04   | 4    | dwParam1   | uint | First processing parameter  
0x08   | 4    | dwParam2   | uint | Second processing parameter
0x0C   | 4    | dwParam3   | uint | Third processing parameter

MessageLogBuffer Structure (partial):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type | Description
0x1F40 | 4    | nTotalRecords   | int  | Total records in this buffer
0x1F44 | 4    | nReadIndex      | int  | Current read position (0-499)
0x1F48 | 4    | pNextBuffer     | ptr  | Pointer to next buffer in chain

0x6FB6CAD0.name: AddPlayerActionToQueue
0x6FB6CAD0.signature: void AddPlayerActionToQueue(int nPlayerId, uint dwActionParam, byte * pbPlayerName, ushort wActionType, ushort wPriority, uint dwData, uint dwTimestamp, ushort wFlags, char * lpszEventName, char * lpszTargetName)
0x6FB6CAD0.comment:
Add player action to the action queue, managing node allocation and queue processing

Algorithm:
1. Validate player ID (-1 triggers fatal error with debug info)
2. Search active queue (DAT_6fbee284) for existing node with matching player ID
3. If found with matching player name, update existing node fields
4. If not found, search free queue (DAT_6fbee288) for available node
5. Allocate new node (0xd5 = 213 bytes) if no free nodes available
6. Initialize node with zero fill (0x21 * 4 = 132 bytes cleared)
7. Set node timestamp via FUN_6fb82290 (system time function)
8. Copy player name to node start with optimized string copy (MOVSD/MOVSB)
9. Set node fields: player ID (+0x10), action param (+0x1c), action type (+0x20), priority (+0x22), data (+0x30), flags (+0x44)
10. Copy event name to node (+0x46) with optimized string copy
11. Copy target name to node (+0x4a) with optimized string copy
12. Set description field (+0x66): player name if event name empty, otherwise formatted string
13. Link node to front of active queue (DAT_6fbee284)
14. Get current player via FUN_6fb62880, extract ID from offset +8
15. Find current player in queue and extract priority (+0x22)
16. Process entire queue with FUN_6fadf420/FUN_6fadf4c0 cleanup operations
17. Execute queue management functions: FUN_6fadf5f0, FUN_6fadf580, FUN_6fadf780, FUN_6fadf480
18. Handle special case for priority -1 with FUN_6fadf7d0
19. Final cleanup with FUN_6fb30200

Parameters:
nPlayerId - Player identifier (int, -1 triggers fatal error)
dwActionParam - Action-specific parameter value (uint)
pbPlayerName - Player name string (byte*, copied to node start)
wActionType - Type of action being queued (ushort, stored at +0x20)
wPriority - Action priority level (ushort, stored at +0x22)
dwData - Additional action data (uint, stored at +0x30)
dwTimestamp - Timestamp parameter (uint, stored at +0x14 but overwritten with FUN_6fb82290)
wFlags - Action flags (ushort, stored at +0x44)
lpszEventName - Event name string (char*, copied to +0x46)
lpszTargetName - Target name string (char*, copied to +0x4a)
IMPLICIT: ECX = nPlayerId, EDX = dwActionParam

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
Player ID -1 triggers fatal error with debug output and program termination
Empty event name causes player name to be copied to description field
Non-empty event name triggers formatted string creation at +0x66

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6fbee284 - Global pointer to active queue head
0x6fbee288 - Global pointer to free queue head  
0x6fbee28c - Global pointer to processing queue
0xd5 (213) - Node allocation size in bytes
0x21 (33) - DWORDs to clear during initialization (132 bytes)
0x10 - Player ID field offset
0x1c - Action parameter field offset
0x20 - Action type field offset  
0x22 - Priority field offset
0x30 - Data field offset
0x34 - Timestamp field offset
0x44 - Flags field offset
0x46 - Event name field offset
0x4a - Target name field offset
0x66 - Description field offset
0x80 - Next pointer field offset
-1 (0xffff) - Default priority when current player not found

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name       Type                Description
0x00    16    playerName      byte[16]            Player name string
0x10    4     playerId        int                 Player identifier
0x1c    4     actionParam     uint                Action parameter
0x20    2     actionType      ushort              Action type code
0x22    2     priority        ushort              Priority level
0x30    4     data            uint                Additional data

0x44    2     flags           ushort              Action flags

0x4a    28    targetName      byte[28]            Target name string
0x66    26    description     byte[26]            Description string
0x80    4     pNext           PlayerActionNode*   Next node pointer

0x6FB6CF30.name: SearchLinkedListForValue
0x6FB6CF30.comment:
Searches a linked list for a specific integer value.

Algorithm:
1. Extract linked list head pointer from UnitAny's list head field at offset +0x38
2. Begin traversal starting from head node
3. Check if current node is NULL (end of list reached)
4. If NULL, return 0 (value not found)
5. Compare current node's data value with search target
6. If values match, return 1 (value found)
7. Advance to next node using next pointer at offset +0x4
8. Repeat from step 3 until match found or list exhausted

Parameters:
pUnit (UnitAny*): Pointer to UnitAny object containing linked list head at offset +0x38
nSearchValue (int): Integer value to search for in linked list nodes

Returns:
1 if search value found in any list node
0 if search value not found or list is empty

Structure Layout:
ListNode (8 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field     Type    Description
+0x0    4     data      int     Node data value
+0x4    4     next      ptr     Pointer to next ListNode

UnitAny with List Head (partial):
Offset  Size  Field     Type         Description  
+0x38   4     listHead  ListNode*    Head pointer of linked list

0x6FB6CF50.name: ProcessEntityPositionUpdate
0x6FB6CF50.signature: void ProcessEntityPositionUpdate(int nEntityId, ushort wXCoord, ushort wYCoord, uint dwParam4, uint dwEntityData)
0x6FB6CF50.comment:
Updates entity position coordinates and reorganizes entity management structures.

Algorithm:
1. Validate entity ID is not -1 (invalid)
2. Search entity management structures (DAT_6fbee284) for matching entity ID
3. Check if entity already exists in child list at offset +0x38
4. If entity found and not duplicate, update coordinates and data:
   - Store X coordinate at offset +0x22
   - Store Y coordinate at offset +0x20  
   - Store entity data at offset +0x30
5. Call FUN_6fae1650() for entity update notification
6. Get current entity ID from FUN_6fb62880() +0x8 offset
7. Search for current entity and extract X coordinate at offset +0x22
8. Process entity cleanup loop - call FUN_6fadf420/FUN_6fadf4c0 on all entities
9. Clear entity management structure (DAT_6fbee284 = 0)
10. Rebuild entity list from DAT_6fbee28c based on sorting mode:
    - If sorting disabled: call FUN_6fadf2e0()
    - If sorting enabled: call FUN_6fadf3a0()
11. Call FUN_6fadf520() for list reorganization
12. If target entity found, move it to front of list
13. Rebuild linked entity structures, linking all nodes via offset +0x80
14. Call cleanup functions FUN_6fadf480() and FUN_6fb30200()
15. If no target entity, call FUN_6fadf7d0() with current entity ID

Parameters:
nEntityId - Entity identifier to update (-1 = invalid)
wXCoord - New X coordinate position  
wYCoord - New Y coordinate position
dwParam4 - Unused parameter (reserved)
dwEntityData - Entity-specific data stored at offset +0x30

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Returns early if nEntityId is -1 (invalid entity)
- Returns early if DAT_6fbee284 is NULL (no entity structures)
- Returns early if entity already exists in child list (duplicate prevention)
- Target entity coordinate extraction returns -1 if entity not found

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type | Description
+0x10  | 4    | dwEntityId    | int  | Primary entity identifier
+0x20  | 2    | wYCoordinate  | short| Y position coordinate
+0x22  | 2    | wXCoordinate  | short| X position coordinate  
+0x30  | 4    | dwEntityData  | uint | Entity-specific data/flags
+0x38  | 4    | pChildList    | ptr  | Pointer to child entity list
+0x80  | 4    | pNextStruct   | ptr  | Pointer to next entity structure

0x6FB6D140.name: CleanupPlayerSlots
0x6FB6D140.comment:
Cleanup and reorganize player slot management structures.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input player ID (-1 triggers fatal error with message)
2. Search and remove matching player node from g_PlayerNodeList
   - Traverse linked list comparing player ID at offset 0x10  
   - Unlink node by updating previous node's next pointer (offset 0x80)
   - Free node's internal lists at offsets 0x34 and 0x38
   - Free the node itself using Ordinal_10043(0x12e)
3. Get current active player ID from game state
4. Search for current player node in list or sublists
5. Build temporary SlotNode list from all remaining player nodes
   - Extract slot ID from offset 0x22 of each player node
   - Create or reuse SlotNode structures via FUN_6fadf400/Ordinal_10042
   - Process slot data using sort mode selection (IsSortingModeEnabled)
6. Execute slot processing via FUN_6fadf520
7. Reorganize slots to prioritize current player's slot
   - Move current player's slot to head of list if found
   - Rebuild main player list from processed slot data  
8. Clean up temporary SlotNode list structures
9. Update player state if no current player (FUN_6fadf7d0)
10. Trigger final update via FUN_6fb30200

Parameters:
nPlayerId (int): Target player ID to cleanup, -1 for invalid/debug mode

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- nPlayerId = -1: Triggers debug assertion with "INVALID_PLAYER_ID" message
- No current player (ID = -1): Calls FUN_6fadf7d0 for state reset
- Missing SlotNode: Creates new structure via Ordinal_10042(0x1f9)

Structure Layout:
PlayerNode (estimated 132+ bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type      Description  
0x10    4     dwPlayerId    uint      Player identifier
0x22    2     wSlotId       ushort    Slot identifier 
0x34    4     pList1        void*     First internal list
0x38    4     pList2        void*     Second internal list  
0x80    4     pNext         void*     Next player node

SlotNode (12 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type      Description
0x0     2     wSlotId       ushort    Slot identifier
0x4     4     pSlotData     void*     Processed slot data
0x8     4     pNext         void*     Next slot node

Global Variables:
g_PlayerNodeList (0x6fbee284): Head of player node linked list
g_SlotNodeList (0x6fbee28c): Head of temporary slot node list

0x6FB6D3B0.name: CleanupPlayerActionQueues
0x6FB6D3B0.comment:
Cleanup and release all player action queue structures and associated memory.

Algorithm:
1. Traverse primary action queue (DAT_6fbee284) linked list by following +0x80 next pointers
2. For each queue node: call FUN_6fb822d0 to cleanup data pointer at +0x34 offset
3. Traverse secondary action list at +0x38 offset, following +0x4 next pointers
4. For each action in secondary list: call Ordinal_10043(0x10d, 0) to free memory blocks
5. Clear queue node's action list pointer (+0x38) and call Ordinal_10043(0x14a, 0) to free node
6. Move to next queue node via +0x80 pointer until end of chain
7. Clear global primary queue head pointer (DAT_6fbee284) 
8. Repeat steps 1-6 for secondary action queue (DAT_6fbee288) using same structure layout
9. Clear global secondary queue head pointer (DAT_6fbee288)

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
Empty queues (NULL globals) are handled gracefully by initial NULL checks
Broken chain links are handled by NULL pointer checks in while loops

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x34 (52) - Offset to data pointer field in queue node structure
0x38 (56) - Offset to action list head pointer in queue node structure  
0x80 (128) - Offset to next queue node pointer in structure
0x4 - Offset to next action pointer in action list node
0x10d (269) - Ordinal for memory deallocation function (likely GlobalFree)
0x14a (330) - Ordinal for queue node deallocation function
0x156 (342) - Ordinal for secondary queue node deallocation function

Structure Layout:
Queue Node Structure (minimum 132 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name           Type    Description
+0x34   4     pData               void*    Pointer to associated data requiring cleanup
+0x38   4     pActionList         void*    Head of linked action list

Offset  Size  Field Name           Type    Description

0x6FB6D480.name: GetPlayerNodeNext
0x6FB6D480.comment:
Retrieves the next player node in a linked list data structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input player node pointer for null check
2. If input pointer is valid (non-null), dereference next pointer at offset 0x80
3. Return the next player node pointer from current node structure
4. If input is null, return global player list head pointer as fallback
5. Handle end-of-list cases where next pointer may be null

Parameters:
pPlayerNode - PlayerSlotNode pointer to current player node in linked list, or null for list head access

Returns:
PlayerSlotNode pointer to next node in the linked list
Returns null when reaching end of list or when next pointer is unset
When input is null, returns global player list head pointer (g_pPlayerListHead)

Special Cases:
Input null: Returns global player list head from g_pPlayerListHead (0x6fbee284)
Next pointer null: Indicates end of linked list traversal
Offset 0x80 (128 decimal): Standard next pointer location in PlayerSlotNode structure

0x6FB6D4A0.name: GetRosterFieldAt0x66
0x6FB6D4A0.comment:
Validates roster pointer and returns pointer to field at offset 0x66.

Algorithm:
1. Check if roster pointer is NULL (pRoster == 0)
2. If NULL, trigger assertion with source file, variable name, and line number
3. Return pointer to field at offset 0x66 from roster base address

Parameters:
pRoster (int): Pointer to roster structure (should be void* but typed as int)

Returns:
int: Pointer to field at offset 0x66 from roster base address
     Returns pRoster + 0x66 (102 decimal)

Special Cases:

- Source file: "C:\Projects\Diablo2\Source\D2Client\GAME\Roster.cpp"
- Variable name: "ptRoster"
- Line number: 0x171 (369 decimal)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x66 (102 decimal): Byte offset to specific field in roster structure
0x171 (369 decimal): Source line number for assertion

0x6FB6D4D0.name: InsertStringIntoSortedTree
0x6FB6D4D0.comment:
Inserts a string node into a lexicographically ordered binary search tree.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input node pointer - return early if NULL
2. Initialize traversal state: previous node as NULL, current node as input
3. Calculate pointer to next field at offset 0x80 from current node
4. Retrieve next node from current->pNext field
5. If no previous node exists, jump to insertion point setup
6. Begin comparison loop with current node's key string
7. Compare characters byte-by-byte using lexicographical ordering
8. For equal characters, advance both string pointers by 2 bytes
9. Continue comparison until null terminator or difference found
10. Calculate comparison result: -1 (less), 0 (equal), 1 (greater)
11. If current key < previous key, traverse to next node in tree
12. Update traversal pointers: parent, iterator, continue search
13. If traversal reaches end (next node is NULL), prepare insertion
14. At insertion point: either root insertion or parent link update
15. For root insertion: set tree root to previous node, link input as next
16. For parent insertion: update parent->pNext to previous->pNext, link nodes
17. Set current node to next node, continue processing if not NULL
18. Return to step 3 for next iteration

Parameters:
pNode (StringTreeNode *): Node to insert containing key string and next pointer

Returns:
void: Function performs in-place tree modification

Special Cases:
NULL input: Function returns immediately without modification
Root insertion: When previous node is NULL, node becomes new tree root
Lexicographical ordering: Comparison uses byte-by-byte string comparison

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type              | Description
0x00   | 128  | szKey      | char[128]         | Null-terminated key string
0x80   | 4    | pNext      | StringTreeNode *  | Pointer to next node in tree

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x80 (128): Offset to pNext field in StringTreeNode structure
0x2: String comparison advancement (2 bytes per iteration)
0x0: NULL pointer constant for tree traversal termination

0x6FB6D590.name: InsertNodeIntoSortedList
0x6FB6D590.comment:
Inserts a node into a sorted linked list maintaining priority order.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize head pointer to NULL for accumulating processed nodes
2. Process all nodes in the incoming linked list chain
3. For each node, get pointer to its next field (offset 0x80)
4. Store next node reference for continued iteration
5. If no head yet established, set current node as new head
6. Otherwise, traverse existing sorted list to find insertion point
7. Compare node priorities (offset 0x18) to maintain ascending order
8. Insert node after last node with higher or equal priority
9. Update list linkage: set current node's next to insertion point's next
10. Set insertion point's next to current node
11. Continue until all nodes processed

Parameters:
pNodeToInsert - Pointer to SortedListNode to insert (may be chain of nodes)

Returns:
void - Function modifies linked list structure in place

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name  | Type              | Description
-------|------|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------
0x00   | 24   | data        | byte[24]         | Node data payload
0x18   | 4    | dwPriority  | uint             | Sort priority (ascending)
0x1C   | 100  | padding1    | byte[100]        | Reserved/padding space
0x80   | 4    | pNext       | SortedListNode * | Pointer to next node

Special Cases:
- NULL input pointer: Function returns immediately with no operation
- Single node: Inserted as new head if list was empty
- Chain insertion: Entire chain processed node by node maintaining individual priorities
- Equal priorities: New nodes inserted after existing nodes with same priority

0x6FB6D5F0.name: FindShortListNode
0x6FB6D5F0.comment:
Search for a node containing a specific short value in a linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize current node pointer to global list head (DAT_6fbee28c)
2. Check if list head is non-null, return null if empty list
3. Begin traversal loop through linked list nodes
4. Compare current node's value (offset 0) with search target
5. If values match, return pointer to current node
6. Load next node pointer from current node (offset 8)
7. Continue loop until next pointer is null
8. Return null if value not found in any node

Parameters:
- nSearchValue: short value to search for in the linked list

Returns:
- void *: Pointer to the node containing the target value, or null if not found

Special Cases:
- Empty list (head is null): Returns null immediately
- Value not in list: Returns null after full traversal
- First node match: Returns immediately without traversal

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type    | Description
-------|------|------------|---------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 2    | value      | short   | Data value for comparison
0x02   | 2    | padding    | short   | Alignment padding
0x04   | 4    | unused     | uint    | Unused field
0x08   | 4    | next       | void *  | Pointer to next node in list

0x6FB6D610.name: FindOrCreateShortListNode
0x6FB6D610.comment:
Searches for a short value in the global short list and creates new node if not found.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global short list head (g_pShortListHead) is null
2. If not null, traverse linked list comparing each node's value to target
3. If matching node found, return immediately (no action needed)
4. If end of list reached without match, proceed to allocation
5. Allocate new 12-byte ShortListNode using Ordinal_10042 (0x1f9 bytes, flag 0)
6. Initialize all 6 short fields to zero (clearing 12-byte structure)
7. Set node's value field to target short value
8. Link new node as new head: node->pNext = old_head, head = node
9. Return (void function)

Parameters:
- nValue (short): Target value to search for in linked list

Returns:
- void: No return value, modifies global list state

Special Cases:
- Empty list (g_pShortListHead == NULL): Skips search, proceeds to allocation
- Value already exists: Early return without allocation (prevents duplicates)
- Memory allocation failure: Function assumes Ordinal_10042 succeeds

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x1f9 (505): Memory allocation size parameter for Ordinal_10042
- 0x0: Flags parameter for Ordinal_10042 (no special allocation flags)
- 0x8: Offset to next pointer field in ShortListNode structure
- 12 bytes: Total ShortListNode structure size (6 shorts)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type    | Description
-------|------|------------|---------|------------------
0x0    | 2    | nValue     | short   | Stored value
0x2    | 2    | wPadding   | ushort  | Alignment padding
0x4    | 4    | reserved1  | uint    | Unused field
0x8    | 4    | pNext      | void*   | Next node pointer

Error Handling:
- No explicit error checking for allocation failure
- Assumes Ordinal_10042 always returns valid pointer
- Function design prevents duplicate values through early return

0x6FB6D670.name: DeallocateRemainingListNodes
0x6FB6D670.comment:
Deallocates all remaining list nodes in the global linked list and calls cleanup routine for each node.

Algorithm:
1. Load global list head pointer from g_pListHead (0x6fbee28c)
2. Check if list is empty (head pointer is NULL)
3. If empty, explicitly set head pointer to NULL and return
4. Traverse linked list using next pointer at offset +8
5. For each node, call Ordinal_10043 cleanup routine with parameters 0x22c and 0
6. Continue until reaching end of list (next pointer is NULL)
7. Set global list head pointer to NULL to mark list as empty

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If list is already empty, function safely returns after setting head to NULL
  - Function assumes all nodes have valid next pointers at offset +8
  - Cleanup routine Ordinal_10043 is called for each node before deallocation

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x22c (556 decimal) - Cleanup operation code parameter for Ordinal_10043
  0x0 - Secondary parameter for Ordinal_10043 cleanup routine
  0x8 - Offset to next pointer in ListNode structure

Structure Layout:
  ListNode (8 bytes):
    Offset  Size  Field Name   Type        Description
    +0x0    4     data         void*       Node data pointer
    +0x4    4     reserved     uint        Reserved field or additional data
    +0x8    4     pNext        ListNode*   Pointer to next node in list

0x6FB6D6B0.name: RemovePlayerNodeFromList
0x6FB6D6B0.comment:
Removes a player node from the global player linked list based on matching player ID.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize previous node tracker to null (pPreviousNode = 0)
2. Load head of global player list (g_pPlayerListHead) into current node pointer
3. Check if list is empty - if so, return immediately
4. Begin traversal loop through linked list nodes
5. Compare player ID at offset +0x22 with target ID from request
6. If IDs match (found target node):
   a. Get pointer to next field (offset +0x80)
   b. Load next node address from current node
   c. If no previous node (removing head):
      - Update global head pointer to next node
      - Set removed node's next to request's storage pointer
      - Store removed node address in request's storage pointer
   d. If has previous node (removing middle/tail):
      - Update previous node's next pointer to skip current node
      - Set removed node's next to request's storage pointer  
      - Store removed node address in request's storage pointer
7. If IDs don't match:
   a. Load next node address from current node's next field
   b. Update previous node tracker to current node
8. Advance to next node and repeat until end of list
9. Return (void function)

Parameters:
pRequest - PlayerRemovalRequest structure containing:
  +0x0: wPlayerIdToFind (ushort) - Player ID to search for and remove
  +0x4: ppRemovedNode (void**) - Pointer to store removed node address

Returns:
void - No return value, operates by side effect on global list and request structure

Special Cases:
- Empty list: Function returns immediately without modification

- Removing head node: Global g_pPlayerListHead updated to new head
- Single node removal: List becomes empty, g_pPlayerListHead set to null

- Previous node tracking for mid-list removal

0x6FB6D710.name: SortShortListNodesAscending
0x6FB6D710.comment:
Sorts the global linked list of ShortListNode items in ascending order by their ushort values.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global list head (g_pShortListHead) is NULL, if so, return immediately
2. Initialize sorted list head pointer to NULL (local accumulator)
3. While global list is not empty:
   a. Remove first node from global list and store as nodeToInsert  
   b. Update global head to next node in chain
   c. If sorted list is empty, insert nodeToInsert as first element
   d. Otherwise, traverse sorted list to find correct insertion position:
      - Compare nodeToInsert value with current node values
      - Find position where nodeToInsert.value < current.value 
      - Insert nodeToInsert before that position
   e. Add nodeToInsert to sorted list at correct position
4. When global list is exhausted, replace global head with sorted list head

Parameters:
- void - Function takes no parameters, operates on global state

Returns:
- void - Function modifies global state (g_pShortListHead) but returns no value

Special Cases:
- Empty list (g_pShortListHead == NULL): Function returns immediately, no sorting needed
- Single node: Node remains in place, no movement required  
- Equal values: Preserves original order (stable sort)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type            | Description
-------|------|------------|-----------------|-----------------------------------
0x0    | 2    | value      | ushort         | Sorting key value
0x8    | 4    | pNext      | ShortListNode* | Pointer to next node in list

Algorithm Implementation:
- Uses classic insertion sort algorithm for linked lists
- Maintains sorted invariant: each insertion preserves ascending order
- Time complexity: O(n²) worst case, O(n) best case for nearly sorted
- Space complexity: O(1) - sorts in-place using existing node structures

0x6FB6D770.name: RemovePlayerActionFromQueue
0x6FB6D770.comment:
Remove a player action from the action queue by player ID and action type.

2. Validate nActionType is not -1 (0xFFFF), return early if invalid
3. Traverse ShortListNode linked list searching for matching nActionType
4. If matching ShortListNode found and has previous node:

   - Move current node to head of global list (reorganization)
5. Access PlayerActionNode list from ShortListNode.pActionList (offset +0x4)  
6. Traverse PlayerActionNode linked list searching for matching nPlayerId (offset +0x10)
7. If matching PlayerActionNode found and has previous node:
   - Remove current node from list by updating previous node's next pointer (offset +0x80)
   - Move current node to head of ShortListNode's action list

0x6FB6D970.name: MergePlayerNodeLists
0x6FB6D970.comment:

   b. If destination list exists, append source node to tail
   c. Clear source node's next pointer to prevent dangling references
   d. Traverse to end of destination list to update tail pointer

0x6FB6D9C0.name: MovePlayerToListHead

      - Set found node's next pointer to current list head
      - Update g_pPlayerListHead to point to found node
   d. Advance: pCurrentNode = current node's next pointer (+0x80)
   e. Update: pPreviousNode = pFoundNode
   f. Continue while pCurrentNode != 0

    - List mode: Insert into sorted list structure

13. If target search value found, move corresponding node to list head
14. Rebuild main player list from sorted short list structure
15. Traverse to end of each player node chain for proper linking

Early exit if g_pPlayerListHead is null (empty list)
Signed flag conversion when bit 15 set: (dwFlags & 0xFFFF) - 0x10000

0x6FB6DEE0.name: ProcessPlayerStateTransition
0x6FB6DEE0.comment:
Process player state transitions and manage player list reorganization

Algorithm:
1. Validate input player state object is non-null
2. Process state transition via switch statement on state field (offset 0x30):
   - State 0 -> 4: Set packet type 0x06 (player join)
   - State 1: Log critical error and terminate with exit code -1
   - State 2 -> 1: Set packet type 0x08 (player leave)  
   - State 3 -> 1: Set packet type 0x09 (player disconnect)
   - State 4 -> 0: Set packet type 0x07 (player rejoin)
3. Log six-byte packet with packet type and player ID (offset 0x10)
4. Retrieve current player ID from game session context
5. Search global player list for matching player ID or child list entries
6. Store target player's short value if found, otherwise use -1
7. Process all players in global list - create short nodes and remove from main list
8. Rebuild player list based on sorting mode (tree or list insertion)
9. Sort all short nodes in ascending order
10. If target player found, move their node to head of short list
11. Reconstruct main player list from short nodes in sorted order
12. Clean up temporary short node list
13. If no target found, move matching player to head of main list
14. Finalize player list state via cleanup function

Parameters:
pPlayerState (PlayerSlotData *): Player state object containing transition info
  - Offset 0x10: Player ID (uint)
  - Offset 0x30: Current state value (uint) - see State Machine below

Returns:
void - No return value, operates on global player list state

Special Cases:
State value 1 triggers critical error termination
Invalid or null input parameter skips all processing
Player ID -1 indicates session context failure
Empty player list skips list processing operations

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x06 - Packet type for player join
0x07 - Packet type for player rejoin  
0x08 - Packet type for player leave
0x09 - Packet type for player disconnect
0x10 - Offset to player ID field
0x22 - Offset to short value field
0x30 - Offset to state field
0x38 - Offset to child list pointer
0x80 - Offset to next player node
0x1F9 - Allocation ID for short nodes
0x22C - Deallocation ID for cleanup
0x4BD - Error code for state 1 termination
-1 - Invalid/not found indicator

State Machine:
State 0: Initial/Join -> State 4 (Active)
State 1: Error -> Terminate (Fatal)
State 2: Leave -> State 1 (Disconnected)
State 3: Disconnect -> State 1 (Disconnected)  
State 4: Active -> State 0 (Rejoining)

Error Handling:
State 1 logs error to debug output and calls exit(-1)
Null player state pointer bypasses all processing
Invalid player IDs default to -1 (not found)
Memory allocation failures not explicitly handled

3. Check nested connection list (offset +0x38) for player ID matches
4. Mark player as disconnected (set flag at +0x30, invalidate value at +0x22 to 0xFFFF)
5. If player not found, log error and terminate with FUN_6fb9a10f
6. Process all players through short list structure for reorganization
7. Remove player nodes from lists using RemovePlayerNodeFromList
8. Sort remaining nodes based on mode: string tree or sorted list
9. Move target player to list head if sVar10 != -1
10. Rebuild player list from short list nodes (link via offset +0x80)
11. Deallocate remaining nodes and update global player list head
12. Log disconnection event with 6-byte packet (type 9, player ID)

None (uses global player context)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Player ID -1 indicates no current player, triggers error path
- Missing player in main list causes application termination
- Target value -1 skips player reordering step

0x30: Player status/flags field (set to 1 on disconnect)

0x6FB6E3A0.name: ProcessPlayerRemovalRequest
0x6FB6E3A0.comment:
Processes player removal request and manages roster state transitions

Algorithm:
1. Validate request pointer is non-NULL, return early if invalid
2. Get game context and check player eligibility for removal based on ID and level threshold
3. If player not eligible (level < 9 and not in active roster), return early
4. Update roster tracking structures and send command 0x5D packet notification
5. Validate action type is not -1 (invalid), return if invalid action
6. Search global player list (g_pPlayerListHead) for target player by mode ID
7. Verify action type matches between request and found player entry
8. Mark player as removed by setting action type to -1 and status to 1
9. Rebuild player roster by processing all active players through short list
10. Sort and reorganize roster data structures using appropriate sorting method
11. Clear player list head and rebuild from sorted short list nodes
12. Deallocate temporary data structures and finalize roster state
13. If action type was unspecified, move player to list head for cleanup

Parameters:
pRequest (PlayerRemovalRequest *): Pointer to player removal request structure containing:
  +0x10: Player ID (DWORD) - unique identifier for target player
  +0x20: Player level (USHORT) - minimum level 9 required for removal eligibility  
  +0x22: Action type (SHORT) - specific removal action (-1 = invalid, others valid)

Returns:
void: No return value, operates through side effects on global roster state

Special Cases:
- Level threshold: Players below level 9 cannot be removed unless already in active roster
- Action type -1: Invalid action, triggers early return without roster changes
- Null player request: Function returns immediately without processing
- Player not found: Triggers fatal error via Ordinal_10023 and FUN_6fb9a10f(-1)
- Action type mismatch: Returns without changes if request action != player action

0xFFFFFFFF: Invalid mode ID sentinel value

0x6FB6E6C0.comment:

0x6FB6EAF0.name: UpdatePlayerDataFields
0x6FB6EAF0.signature: void UpdatePlayerDataFields(int nPlayerId, int nDataValue1, int nDataValue2)
0x6FB6EAF0.comment:

  nDataValue2 (Stack[0x4]): Second data value to store at offset 0x40

Returns:
  void - No return value, function operates by side effect

Special Cases:
  - Player ID of -1 is invalid and causes immediate return
  - NULL player list head causes immediate return
  - NULL player node during search causes safe exit
  - Function handles two-level list structure (main list + sub-lists)

0x6FB6EB40.name: FindPlayerDataByPlayerId
0x6FB6EB40.comment:
Searches the player list for a player by ID and returns pointer to player data.

Algorithm:
1. Load head of player list from g_pPlayerListHead global
2. If list is empty (NULL), return 0 (not found)
3. Traverse linked list using next pointer at offset +0x80
4. For each node, check two player ID fields at offsets +0x3c and +0x40
5. If either ID matches nPlayerId parameter, return pointer to data at offset +0x66
6. Continue until end of list or match found
7. Return 0 if player not found

Parameters:
nPlayerId (int) - Player ID to search for in the list

Returns:
PlayerListNode * - Pointer to player data structure at offset +0x66 from node base
NULL (0) - Player ID not found in list

Structure Layout:
PlayerListNode (154 bytes total):
Offset  Size  Field Name          Type    Description
+0x3c   4     dwPlayerId1         uint    Primary player identifier
+0x40   4     dwPlayerId2         uint    Secondary player identifier  
+0x66   ?     playerData          ?       Player data structure (return offset)
+0x80   4     pNext               ptr     Next node in linked list

Special Cases:
- Function checks TWO player ID fields per node (+0x3c and +0x40)
- Returns pointer offset +0x66 bytes from node base, not node base itself
- Uses __fastcall convention with nPlayerId passed in ECX register

0x6FB6EB70.name: CheckPlayerIdConflict
0x6FB6EB70.comment:
Checks for conflicting player connections in the player list

Algorithm:
1. Extract player ID from input parameter using offset 0x8
2. Call GetPlayerId function to retrieve player ID value  
3. Return 0 (no conflict) if player ID is -1 (invalid)
4. Return 0 (no conflict) if player list head is null
5. Traverse player linked list starting from g_pPlayerListHead
6. For each node, check if player ID matches extracted ID
7. If IDs match but player field at offset 0x10 differs, return 1 (conflict found)
8. Continue to next node using pointer at offset 0x80
9. Return 0 (no conflict) if end of list reached without finding conflict

Parameters:
- pPlayerData: Pointer to player data structure containing player information

Returns:
- 1 if conflicting player found (same ID but different field value)
- 0 if no conflict found or invalid input

Special Cases:
- Player ID -1 indicates invalid/disconnected player (no conflict)
- Empty player list (g_pPlayerListHead == null) results in no conflict
- Function stops at first conflict found, does not count total conflicts

0x6FB6EBB0.name: GetPlayerDataById
0x6FB6EBB0.comment:
Search player list by ID and retrieve associated data value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate player ID is not -1 (invalid marker)
2. Check if global player list head is initialized
3. Iterate through main player list (PlayerListNode chain)
4. For each main player node, compare ID field at offset 0x10 with target
5. If main node matches, return data value from offset 0x34
6. If no main node match, search nested sub-list at offset 0x38
7. Iterate through sub-list (PlayerSubNode chain linked at offset 0x4)
8. For each sub-node, compare ID at offset 0x0 with target
9. If sub-node matches, return data value from main node offset 0x34
10. Continue to next main player node via offset 0x80 link
11. Return 0 if no matching player ID found

Parameters:
  nPlayerId - int: Player identifier to search for (-1 = invalid)

Returns:
  uint: Player data value from PlayerListNode offset 0x34, or 0 if not found

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 immediately if nPlayerId is -1
  - Returns 0 if g_pPlayerListHead is NULL (empty list)
  - Returns 0 if matching player node pointer becomes NULL (corrupted list)

0x6FB6EBF0.name: ProcessPlayerListUpdateWithSorting
0x6FB6EBF0.comment:
Sets a player's priority value and completely reorganizes the player list with special positioning.

Algorithm:

1. Validate input player ID is not -1, return early if invalid
2. Search player list (g_pPlayerListHead) for player matching nPlayerId
3. Search sub-nodes at offset 0x38 if main player ID doesn't match
4. Return early if player not found in list or sub-nodes
5. Store sPriorityValue at offset 0x22 in found player structure
6. Call FUN_6fb62880() to get priority player ID from system state
7. Search for priority player in list and save their current priority value (sVar9)
8. Process all players in list to create short list nodes for reorganization
9. For each player, find or create ShortListNode with their priority value
10. Remove all players from main list using RemovePlayerNodeFromList()
11. Re-sort and re-insert all players based on current sorting mode
12. Call SortShortListNodesAscending() to order by priority values
13. If priority player exists (sVar9 != -1), move them to list head
14. Reconstruct main player list from sorted short list in priority order
15. Handle special positioning for priority player found in step 6-7
16. Clean up temporary short list nodes with DeallocateRemainingListNodes()
17. If no priority player found, move system priority player to head
18. Call FUN_6fb30200() for final list state update

Parameters:

nPlayerId (int): Target player ID to update priority for (-1 = invalid)
sPriorityValue (short): New priority value to store at offset 0x22

Returns:

void - Function modifies global player list state

Special Cases:

Player ID -1 triggers early return without processing
Missing player in list/sub-nodes triggers early return
Priority player value -1 indicates no special positioning needed
Empty player list (g_pPlayerListHead == 0) triggers early return

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x10 - Player ID field offset in PlayerListNode structure
0x22 - Priority value field offset (16-bit short value)
0x38 - Sub-nodes pointer offset for player search
0x80 - Next player pointer offset in linked list
0x1f9 - Allocation ID for short list node creation
-1 (0xFFFF) - Invalid/unset priority value indicator

0x6FB6EDF0.name: SetPlayerPaddingFieldById
0x6FB6EDF0.comment:
Search player list by ID and set padding field value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input: Return early if player ID is -1 or player list head is null
2. Traverse main player list starting from g_pPlayerListHead
3. For each player node, check if nPlayerId matches target ID
4. If match found in main list, jump to field update logic
5. If no match, traverse sub-node list for current player
6. Check each sub-node for matching player ID
7. If match found in sub-list, jump to field update logic
8. Move to next player node via abTargetData[4] offset (+0x80)
9. Continue until end of list reached
10. When match found: Validate player node is not null
11. Mask padding value to 8-bit range (& 0xFF)
12. Store masked value in dwPadding8 field (+0x30 offset)
13. Call FUN_6fb30200() for post-update processing

Parameters:
nPlayerId (int): Target player ID to search for (-1 indicates invalid)
dwPaddingValue (uint): Value to store in padding field (masked to byte)

Returns:
void - No return value, operates by side effect

Special Cases:
Player ID -1 treated as invalid input and causes early return
Null player list head causes early return without processing
Null player node after match found causes early return without update
Padding value automatically masked to 0xFF range before storage

0x6FB6EE40.name: ProcessPlayerNetworkAction
0x6FB6EE40.signature: void ProcessPlayerNetworkAction(int nPlayerId, int nActionType, uint dwActionData)
0x6FB6EE40.comment:
Process network action for a specific player by searching the player list hierarchy.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input player ID (must not be -1) and global player list exists
2. Search main player list nodes for matching player ID
3. If player not found in main node, search sub-node list iteratively  
4. If player found in sub-nodes, jump to processing section
5. Continue to next main player node via next pointer (+0x80 offset)
6. Repeat search until player found or list exhausted
7. When player found, validate player node is not null
8. Call FUN_6fb82310 with player ID and action type for initialization
9. Call FUN_6fb82420 with player ID, action type, and masked action data (0xFFFF)
10. Call FUN_6fb30200 for global state synchronization
11. Call FUN_6fb62880 to get game state handle
12. Validate action type matches game state handle offset +0x8
13. If validation passes, call FUN_6fae1880 with player ID for finalization

Parameters:
  nPlayerId (int): Unique player identifier to search for (-1 = invalid)
  nActionType (int): Type of network action to process  
  dwActionData (uint): Action-specific data payload (only lower 16 bits used)

Returns:
  void: Function performs side effects, no return value

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if nPlayerId is -1 (invalid player)
  - Returns early if global player list head is null
  - Returns early if player node becomes null during processing  
  - Returns early if action type validation fails against game state

0x6FB6EEC0.name: AddPlayerToRosterWithBody
0x6FB6EEC0.comment:
Adds a player to the roster list and associates a body/unit ID with them.

If the player ID already exists in the roster (either as a primary node or in a
sub-node list), uses the existing node. Otherwise, allocates a new PlayerListNode
(132 bytes), zero-initializes it, and prepends it to the secondary roster list
(g_pRosterListHead). Then ensures the body ID is linked to the player's sub-node list.

Algorithm:
1. If nPlayerId == -1, skip search and create new node
2. Search g_pPlayerListHead linked list for matching player ID
3. For each node, also search its sub-node list (offset 0x38) for matching ID
4. If found, use existing node; otherwise allocate new 0x84-byte PlayerListNode
5. Zero-initialize new node with REP STOSD (0x21 dwords = 132 bytes)
6. Set node's nPlayerId field at offset 0x10
7. Link new node into g_pRosterListHead list via offset 0x80
8. Search node's sub-node list for matching nBodyId
9. If nBodyId not found, allocate 8-byte sub-node (id + next pointer)
10. Zero-initialize sub-node, set id to nBodyId, prepend to sub-node list

Parameters:
  nPlayerId (ECX) - Player ID to find or create roster entry for (-1 for always new)
  nBodyId (EDX) - Body/unit ID to associate with the player's sub-node list

Returns:
  void

Structure Layout (PlayerListNode, 132 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field            Description
  0x00    16    dwUnknown0-3     Zero-initialized fields
  0x10    4     nPlayerId        Player identifier
  0x14    36    ...              Additional fields
  0x38    4     pSubNodeList     Pointer to linked list of body IDs (8-byte nodes)
  0x3C    68    abTargetData     Target/position data
  0x80    4     pNextNode        Pointer to next PlayerListNode

Sub-node structure (8 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field            Description
  0x00    4     nBodyId          Body/unit identifier
  0x04    4     pNext            Pointer to next sub-node

Error Handling:
  - FogAssert with "ptRoster" if main node allocation fails, then exit(-1)
  - FogAssert with "ptBody" if sub-node allocation fails, then exit(-1)

Special Cases:
  - nPlayerId == -1: Always creates new node without searching
  - Existing node found: Reuses node, only adds body ID if not already present

0x6FB6EFC0.name: RemovePlayerSubNodeFromRoster
0x6FB6EFC0.comment:
Removes a PlayerSubNode from a player's roster linked list.

Searches the global player list (g_pPlayerListHead) to find a PlayerListNode
matching nPlayerId, then searches that node's sub-list (offset 0x38) to find
and unlink a PlayerSubNode matching nSubNodeId.

Algorithm:
1. Load g_pPlayerListHead into ESI, initialize EDI to NULL (previous pointer)
2. If nPlayerId is -1, exit early (invalid ID)
3. If g_pPlayerListHead is NULL, exit (no player list)
4. Compare PlayerListNode.field_0x10 with nPlayerId
5. If not match, search sub-list at offset 0x38:
   a. Load sub-list head from [ESI + 0x38]
   b. Walk sub-list comparing [node + 0x0] with nPlayerId
   c. Follow next pointer at [node + 0x4]
6. If not found in sub-list, follow PlayerListNode.field_0x80 to next node
7. Once player node found, search its sub-list for nSubNodeId:
   a. Load sub-list from [ESI + 0x38]
   b. Compare [node + 0x0] with nSubNodeId
   c. Track previous node in EDI for unlinking
8. If sub-node found:
   a. If EDI != NULL: [EDI + 0x4] = [ECX + 0x4] (unlink from middle)
   b. If EDI == NULL: [ESI + 0x38] = [ECX + 0x4] (unlink from head)
   c. Call ReleasePoolAllocation(ECX, 0x6fbb00d4, 0x6b3, 0) to free node

Parameters:
  nPlayerId (ECX): Player ID to search for in PlayerListNode list
  nSubNodeId (EDX): Sub-node ID to find and remove from sub-list

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - nPlayerId == -1: Early exit, no action
  - g_pPlayerListHead == NULL: Early exit, no player data
  - Player not found: Silent exit
  - Sub-node not found: Silent exit

Structure Layout (PlayerListNode):
  Offset  Size  Field                 Description
  0x10    4     nPlayerId             Player identifier for matching
  0x38    4     pSubNodeListHead      Pointer to PlayerSubNode linked list
  0x80    4     pNextPlayerListNode   Next node in player list

Structure Layout (PlayerSubNode):
  Offset  Size  Field       Description
  0x00    4     nNodeId     Node identifier for matching
  0x04    4     pNext       Next node in sub-list

Magic Numbers:
  0x6b3 (1715): Pool allocation line number for debugging
  0x6fbb00d4: Pool allocator context pointer

0x6FB6F040.name: CheckPlayerPermission
0x6FB6F040.comment:
Checks if requesting player has permission for target player operations

Algorithm:
1. Validate target player ID is not -1 (invalid ID check)
2. Verify global player list head is initialized and not null
3. Iterate through main player list searching for target player ID:
   a. Compare current node's player ID with target player ID
   b. If match found, jump to permission check logic
   c. If no direct match, search sub-node list recursively:
      - Traverse linked list of sub-nodes using next pointer at offset +4
      - Compare each sub-node's player ID with target player ID
      - If found in sub-node list, jump to permission check logic
   d. Move to next player node using pointer at offset 0x80 (abTargetData + 4)
4. Permission check logic (LAB_6fae0e83):
   a. Verify player node pointer is not null (safety check)
   b. Compare requesting player ID with found player's ID
   c. If IDs match (same player), return 1 (permission granted)
   d. If different players, call permission validation function
   e. Return permission check result (1 if granted, 0 if denied)
5. Return 0 if target player not found in any list

Parameters:
nRequestingPlayerId (ECX) - Player ID making the permission request
nTargetPlayerId (EDX) - Player ID for which permission is being checked

Returns:
1 (dword) - Permission granted or same player
0 (dword) - Permission denied or target player not found

Special Cases:
Target player ID -1 returns 0 (invalid player ID)
Null player list head returns 0 (uninitialized system)
Same requesting and target player returns 1 (self-permission)
Player not found in main or sub-node lists returns 0

PlayerListNode structure accessed at multiple offsets:
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type              | Description
0x10   | 4    | nPlayerId       | int               | Unique player identifier
0x38   | 4    | pSubNodeList    | int *             | Pointer to sub-node linked list
0x80   | 4    | Next Node Ptr   | PlayerListNode *  | Pointer to next player (via abTargetData + 4)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Invalid player ID constant
0x10 (16) - Offset to nPlayerId field in PlayerListNode
0x38 (56) - Offset to pSubNodeList field in PlayerListNode  
0x80 (128) - Offset to abTargetData field in PlayerListNode
0x04 (4) - Next pointer offset within abTargetData field
0x01 (1) - Permission check flag parameter to validation function

0x6FB6F0A0.name: CheckPlayersHaveSameTargetArea
0x6FB6F0A0.comment:
Checks if two players exist in the player list and have the same target area ID.

Algorithm:
1. Validate first player ID is not -1 and player list exists
2. Search player list for first player ID in main nodes and subnodes
3. Set pPlayer1Node to found node or NULL if not found
4. Validate second player ID is not -1 and player list exists
5. Search player list for second player ID in main nodes and subnodes  
6. Set pPlayer2Node to found node or NULL if not found
7. If both players found, compare target area IDs at offset +0x22
8. Return 1 if both players exist and have matching non-negative target areas
9. Return 0 if either player not found or target areas don't match

Parameters:
nPlayer1Id - First player identifier to search for
nPlayer2Id - Second player identifier to search for

Returns:
1 - Both players found and have matching target area IDs
0 - Either player not found or target areas don't match or invalid

Special Cases:
Player ID -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) is treated as invalid and skips search
Target area ID -1 (0xFFFF) is treated as invalid even if both players have it
Search includes both main player nodes and their associated subnodes

0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Invalid player ID marker
0xFFFF (-1) - Invalid target area ID marker

0x38 - PlayerListNode.pSubNodeList offset  
0x80 - Next PlayerListNode offset (abTargetData + 4)
0x22 - Target area ID offset in PlayerListNode (dwPadding4 + 2)

Offset  Size  Field Name        Type                Description

0x22    2     wTargetAreaId     short              Target area/level ID
0x38    4     pSubNodeList      int*               Pointer to subnode list  
0x80    4     pNextNode         PlayerListNode*    Next node in main list

Returns 0 for any validation failure or search miss

Gracefully handles NULL pointers in list traversal

0x6FB6F130.name: CheckPlayersForCondition
0x6FB6F130.comment:
Checks all players in the linked list against a specific condition.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize player node pointer to global player list head (g_pPlayerListHead)
2. Call FUN_6fb62880() to get context object and extract value at offset +8
3. Return 0 immediately if player list is empty (null head pointer)
4. Iterate through each player node in the linked list:
   a. Extract player ID from current node (offset 0x10)
   b. Call FUN_6fb823e0(playerId, contextValue, 8) to check condition
   c. Return 1 immediately if condition check returns non-zero (condition met)
   d. Advance to next player node via link at offset 0x80
5. Return 0 if all players checked and none met the condition

Parameters:
None - Function takes no parameters and operates on global player list

Returns:
1 (uint) - At least one player met the specified condition
0 (uint) - No players met the condition or player list is empty

Special Cases:
- Empty player list (g_pPlayerListHead is null) returns 0 immediately
- First player meeting condition causes immediate return of 1
- Function short-circuits on first match for efficiency

Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description

0x80   | 4    | pNext      | PlayerListNode* | Pointer to next node in list

0x6FB6F170.name: CompareUnitIdentifiers
0x6FB6F170.comment:
Compare unit identifiers for matching entities.

Algorithm:

1. Retrieve the current context object/reference unit from global state
2. Validate both input unit and context unit are non-null
3. Extract 8-byte identifier from pUnit at offset 0x10 (qwGuid field)
4. Extract 8-byte identifier from context unit at offset 0x8 (qwGuid field)  
5. Compare the two 8-byte identifiers using memcmp with length 8
6. Return 1 if identifiers match exactly, 0 if different or validation failed

pUnit - Pointer to UnitData structure to compare against context unit

Returns:

1 - Unit identifiers match exactly
0 - Identifiers differ, or null pointer validation failed

Special Cases:

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x8 - Offset to identifier field in context unit structure  
8 - Length of identifier comparison (8 bytes, likely 64-bit GUID)

Error Handling:

Null pointer validation for both input unit and context unit before comparison
Returns 0 for any validation failure or identifier mismatch

0x6FB6F1A0.name: SetPlayerFlagById
0x6FB6F1A0.comment:
Sets a flag value for a player by searching through the player list hierarchy.

Algorithm:
1. Validate player ID is not -1 (invalid)
2. Validate global player list head exists
3. Iterate through main player list nodes
4. For each node, check if nPlayerId matches target
5. If no match, iterate through sub-node list at node->pSubNodeList
6. Check each sub-node ID against target player ID
7. If match found (main or sub), set dwPadding1 field to masked flag value
8. Mask flag value with 0xff to ensure single byte storage
9. Exit immediately after setting flag

Parameters:
nPlayerId (int): Target player ID to search for (-1 is invalid)
nFlagValue (int): Flag value to set, will be masked to single byte (0xff)

Returns:
void: No return value, silently fails if player not found

Special Cases:
- Player ID -1 is treated as invalid and causes immediate return
- NULL global player list head causes immediate return
- Player not found results in no action (silent failure)
- Flag value automatically masked to 0xff for byte storage

0x6FB6F1F0.name: GetPlayerNodePaddingById
0x6FB6F1F0.comment:
Search player list for specified player ID and return padding value from matching node.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input player ID is not -1 (invalid)
2. Check global player list head is not null
3. Iterate through main player list nodes
4. For each node, compare nPlayerId field against target ID
5. If no match in main node, iterate through sub-node list

Returns:
Player node padding value (dwPadding1) if found and not current player
0 if player ID is invalid, not found, or matches current player context

Player ID -1 is treated as invalid and causes immediate return of 0
If target player matches current player context from FUN_6fb62880, return 0

0x6FB6FEC0.name: HandlePacketCreateMonster
0x6FB6FEC0.comment:
Network packet handler for creating a monster unit on the client.

Algorithm:
1. Extract unit creation parameters from packet data structure
2. Call AllocateAndInitializeUnit with extracted parameters:
   - dwUnitType from pPacketData+2 (4 bytes)
   - dwUnitClass from pPacketData+6 (1 byte)
   - wRoomX from pPacketData+7 (2 bytes)
   - wRoomY from pPacketData+9 (2 bytes)
   - nUnitMode from pPacketData+1 (1 byte)
   - Reserved parameter = 0
3. If allocation succeeds and unit type is monster (1), update graphics
4. Return (no return value)

Parameters:
pPacketData (ECX) - Pointer to network packet data with monster creation info:
  +0x00: byte - Packet ID (0x0B for create monster)
  +0x01: byte - Unit mode/action state
  +0x02: uint - Unit type identifier (should be 1 for monster)
  +0x06: byte - Monster class ID
  +0x07: ushort - Room X coordinate
  +0x09: ushort - Room Y coordinate
  Packet size: 11 bytes (0x0B)

Returns:
void - Unit created and registered internally by AllocateAndInitializeUnit

Special Cases:
- If allocation fails (returns NULL), no graphics update occurs
- If allocated unit is not type 1 (monster), graphics update is skipped
- This allows the function to be used for non-monster creation without side effects

Classification: Callback/Handler - packet message handler in function pointer table at 0x6fbb027c
Message ID: 0x0B (11) - Create Monster packet

0x6FB6FF80.name: HandleUnitStateMessage

2. Zero-initialize all 7 elements using REP STOSD
3. Extract first parameter byte from pbMessage[7] into adParams[0]
4. Extract second parameter byte from pbMessage[8] into adParams[1]

7. Return

- pbMessage (byte*, EDX): Pointer to network message packet
  - pbMessage[6]: Operation type byte (0-4, see DispatchUnitStateAction)
  - pbMessage[7]: First parameter byte (stored in adParams[0])
  - pbMessage[8]: Second parameter byte (stored in adParams[1])

Returns:
- void: No return value. State changes are applied via DispatchUnitStateAction.

  Offset 6: Operation type (byte) - determines which handler executes
  Offset 7: Param 1 (byte) - meaning depends on operation type
  Offset 8: Param 2 (byte) - meaning depends on operation type

0x6FB6FFC0.name: ProcessUnitStatePacket
0x6FB6FFC0.comment:
Process incoming unit state action packet and optionally set player flag.

Algorithm:
1. Extract action parameters from packet structure:
   - wActionX from pPacket+0x7 (ushort)
   - wActionY from pPacket+0x9 (ushort)
   - nPlayerId from pPacket+0x2 (dword)
   - byActionParam from pPacket+0xB (byte)
   - byUnitType from pPacket+0x6 (byte)
2. Build parameter array [dwActionX, dwActionY, dwActionParam] on stack
3. Call DispatchUnitStateAction(byUnitType, pUnit, pParams, 1) to process action
4. Check condition byte at pPacket+0x1:
   - If zero: call SetPlayerFlagById(nPlayerId, pPacket+0xC) to set player flag
   - If non-zero: skip flag setting
5. Return

Parameters:
- pUnit (UnitAny*, ECX): Target unit for state action dispatch
- pPacket (byte*, EDX): Pointer to packet structure containing:
  +0x01: byCondition - if 0, set player flag after dispatch
  +0x02: nPlayerId (dword) - player ID for flag setting
  +0x06: byUnitType (byte) - unit type for dispatch
  +0x07: wActionX (ushort) - X coordinate or first param
  +0x09: wActionY (ushort) - Y coordinate or second param  
  +0x0B: byActionParam (byte) - additional action parameter
  +0x0C: byFlagValue (byte) - flag value for SetPlayerFlagById

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- If byCondition at pPacket+0x1 is non-zero, SetPlayerFlagById is skipped
- Action dispatch always executed regardless of condition byte

Callees:
- DispatchUnitStateAction: Dispatches unit action based on type (0x6fb863a0)
- SetPlayerFlagById: Sets flag on player node by ID (0x6fae1060)

2. Tail-jump to internal quest buffer copy routine

Returns:

  - Tail-call optimization - shares stack frame with target function

0x6FB70BE0.name: HandleUnitMovementPacket
0x6FB70BE0.comment:
Parses a unit movement network packet and updates unit position and stats.

Classification: Callback/Handler - Network packet handler for unit movement synchronization

Algorithm:
1. Initialize bit buffer with 9 bytes of packet data
2. Skip 8-bit packet header (message type identifier)
3. Read 15-bit stat value (experience or stamina scaled value)
4. Read 16-bit current X coordinate
5. Read 16-bit current Y coordinate  
6. Read 8-bit signed X velocity/delta
7. Read 8-bit signed Y velocity/delta
8. Get current game context (player unit)
9. If unit is valid:
   a. Set unit stat 10 with scaled stat value (value << 8)
   b. Convert 8-bit deltas to signed values (subtract 0x100 if > 0x80)
   c. Calculate target X = current X + signed delta X
   d. Calculate target Y = current Y + signed delta Y
   e. Call ValidateAndProcessUnitMovement with coordinates

Parameters:
  pbPacketData - byte* [ECX] Pointer to 9-byte network packet buffer

Returns: void

Bit Field Layout (72 bits / 9 bytes):
  Offset  Bits  Field
  0       8     Packet type header (discarded)
  8       15    Stat value (experience/stamina)
  23      16    Current X coordinate
  39      16    Current Y coordinate
  55      8     Signed X delta (-128 to 127)
  63      8     Signed Y delta (-128 to 127)

Magic Numbers:
  0x0A (10) - Stat ID for SetUnitStat (stamina/experience related)
  0x80 - Signed byte threshold for delta conversion
  0x100 - Subtraction value for signed conversion

Special Cases:
  - Returns immediately if GetGameContext returns NULL (no active unit)
  - Delta values > 0x80 are converted to negative (two's complement style)

0x6FB70CE0.name: ConfigureUnitGraphics
0x6FB70CE0.comment:
Configure unit graphics rendering and display parameters

Algorithm:
1. Extract mode value from unit structure at offset +0x7 (2-byte word)
2. Call FUN_6fb60e10 to retrieve graphics data structure using unit's class ID (+0x3 offset)
3. Call D2COMMON.DLL ordinal 10953 to configure primary graphics settings
   - Pass graphics data pointer, mode value, and unit parameters from offsets +0x9 and +0x2
4. Call D2COMMON.DLL ordinal 11030 to configure secondary graphics settings
   - Pass graphics data pointer, mode value, and unit parameter from offset +0xa
5. Call FUN_6fb4ea70 to finalize graphics configuration (tail call optimization)

Parameters:
pUnit (int *): Pointer to unit data structure containing graphics configuration
  IMPLICIT ECX: Unit pointer passed via fastcall register

Returns:
void: Function performs configuration and returns nothing

Special Cases:
- Function uses offsets +0x2, +0x3, +0x7, +0x9, +0xa from unit structure
- Tail call optimization used for final graphics finalization step
- D2COMMON.DLL ordinals suggest Diablo II game engine integration

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name       Type    Description
+0x2    1     byParameter1     byte    First parameter for graphics config
+0x3    4     dwClassId        uint    Unit class identifier for graphics lookup
+0x7    2     wMode            ushort  Graphics display mode
+0x9    1     byParameter2     byte    Second parameter for graphics config  
+0xa    1     byParameter3     byte    Third parameter for graphics config

0x6FB70D30.name: HandleSkillUpdatePacket
0x6FB70D30.comment:
Parse skill update network packet and apply skill delta to matching unit.

Classification: Packet Handler - processes incoming server message for skill modifications.

Algorithm:

1. Extract signed skill delta from packet byte[5] with sign extension (-128 to 127)
2. Extract unit type filter from packet byte[6]
3. Extract skill state filter from packet byte[7]
4. Look up target unit by GUID from packet bytes[1-4] via FindUnitInHashTable
5. If unit found, apply skill delta via ProcessUnitActiveSkills with filters

Parameters:

pbPacketData - Pointer to raw packet data buffer (passed in ECX via __fastcall)

Packet Structure (8 bytes minimum):

Offset | Size | Field              | Description
-------|------|--------------------|----------------------------------
+0x00  |  1   | byOpcode           | Packet opcode (not parsed here)
+0x01  |  4   | dwUnitGUID         | Unit GUID to look up in hash table
+0x05  |  1   | nSignedDelta       | Signed skill delta (-128 to +127)
+0x06  |  1   | byUnitTypeFilter   | Unit type filter (0 = all types)
+0x07  |  1   | bySkillStateFilter | Skill state filter (4 = all states)

Returns:

void - No return value

Special Cases:

- If unit GUID lookup fails, function silently returns without processing
- Delta byte is treated as signed: values > 0x80 are sign-extended to negative
- Sign extension: nDelta = byte - 0x100 when byte > 0x80 (e.g., 0xFF becomes -1)

Callees:

- FindUnitInHashTable: Locates UnitAny by GUID (param_2=0 for type filter)
- ProcessUnitActiveSkills: Applies delta to skills matching filter criteria

0x6FB70D80.name: ProcessUnitSkillListPacket
0x6FB70D80.comment:
Processes a network packet containing a list of skills to set on a unit.

Classification: Packet Handler - processes server-to-client skill list update

Packet Structure (variable length):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  +0x00   1     byOpcode      Packet opcode (not accessed here)
  +0x01   1     bySkillCount  Number of skill entries in packet
  +0x02   4     dwUnitGUID    Unit GUID to look up
  +0x06   3*N   SkillEntries  Array of skill entries (N = bySkillCount)

Skill Entry Structure (3 bytes each):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  +0x00   2     wSkillId      Skill ID
  +0x02   1     bySkillLevel  Skill level to set

Algorithm:
  1. Extract skill count from packet offset +1
  2. Get pointer to skill entries at packet offset +6
  3. Look up unit by GUID from packet offset +2 using FindUnitInHashTable
  4. If unit found and skill count > 0:
     5. Loop through each skill entry:
        a. Read skill ID (2 bytes) and level (1 byte)
        b. Call SetUnitSkillLevel(pUnit, wSkillId, byLevel, 0)
        c. Advance pointer by 3 bytes to next entry
        d. Decrement counter and repeat until zero

Parameters:
  pbPacketData (ECX): Pointer to raw packet data

Returns: void

Loop Details:
  Counter: uVar2 (unsigned), initialized from bySkillCount
  Bounds: [bySkillCount, 0), decrements to zero
  Stride: 3 bytes per skill entry
  Exit: uVar2 == 0

Special Cases:
  - If unit not found in hash table, returns immediately without error
  - If skill count is 0, loop body never executes
  - Fourth parameter to SetUnitSkillLevel is always 0 (unknown flag)

0x6FB71190.name: ParseAndDispatchNetworkMessage
0x6FB71190.comment:
Parses a variable-length network message packet and dispatches it to ProcessNetworkMessage.

Copies packet header fields (10 bytes fixed) and two variable-length strings from
the input buffer into a local stack structure, then passes it to ProcessNetworkMessage.

Classification: Worker function - performs packet parsing before dispatch

Algorithm:
1. Copy fixed header bytes: MsgType (offset 0), SubType (1), Flags (2), Reserved (3)
2. Copy sequence number (offset 4-7, 4 bytes)
3. Copy option bytes: Option1 (offset 8), Option2 (offset 9)
4. Copy first string from offset 10 (max 16 chars) to local buffer
5. Calculate length of first string using SStrLen
6. Copy second string from (offset 10 + strlen + 1) with max 256 chars
7. Call ProcessNetworkMessage with pointer to local structure

Parameters:
  pbPacketData (ECX) - Pointer to raw network packet buffer containing:
    - Fixed 10-byte header
    - Two null-terminated strings (variable length)

Returns: void

Stack Structure Layout (local_11c at ESP):
  Offset  Size  Field        Type    Description
  0x00    1     byMsgType    byte    Message type identifier
  0x01    1     bySubType    byte    Message subtype
  0x02    1     byFlags      byte    Message flags
  0x03    1     byReserved   byte    Reserved/padding
  0x04    4     dwSequence   uint    Sequence number or timestamp
  0x08    1     byOption1    byte    Additional option byte 1
  0x09    1     byOption2    byte    Additional option byte 2
  0x0A    16    szSource     char[]  First string (max 16 chars)
  0x1A    258   szPayload    char[]  Second string (max 256 chars)

Input Packet Format:
  Bytes 0-9: Fixed header (copied directly)
  Bytes 10+: First null-terminated string (player/source name)
  After first string null: Second null-terminated string (message/payload)

0x6FB71210.name: ClearUnitPathMemory
0x6FB71210.comment:
Clears path-related memory for a unit identified by GUID and type.

Classification: Wrapper function

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 8-byte stack frame for unit identifier copy
2. Copy 4-byte unit GUID from input pointer offset +0x0
3. Copy 2-byte unit type from input pointer offset +0x4
4. Pass pointer to stack copy to FUN_6fb58680 for processing
5. Clean up stack and return

Parameters:
  pUnitId (ECX) - Pointer to 6-byte unit identifier structure:
                  +0x0: DWORD unit GUID
                  +0x4: WORD unit type

Returns: void

Called By: No direct callers detected (may be callback or table entry)

Calls: FUN_6fb58680 - Finds unit in hash table and frees memory at offset 0xC8

Notes:
- The 6-byte structure is copied to stack before call, suggesting the
  callee may modify it or the original may become invalid
- FUN_6fb58680 looks up unit by (type, guid) and frees piVar1[0x32] (offset 0xC8)
- Offset 0xC8 in unit structure likely holds path or AI state pointer

0x6FB71260.name: ForwardGameEventMessageCopy
0x6FB71260.comment:
Forwards a game event message by making a stack copy before processing.

Wrapper that copies a 40-byte (10 DWORD) event message structure from the
input pointer to a local stack buffer, then passes the copy to
ProcessGameEventMessage. This ensures the caller's message buffer remains
unmodified during message processing.

Function Classification: Thunk/Wrapper

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 40 bytes (0x28) on stack for local message copy
2. Use REP MOVSD to copy 10 DWORDs from pEventMsg to stack buffer
3. Call ProcessGameEventMessage with pointer to local copy
4. Clean up stack and return

Parameters:

                    (10 DWORDs). Caller retains ownership; data is copied.

Returns:

Special Cases:

  - No validation performed on input pointer

0x6FB71290.name: CopyAndProcessNetValidationData
0x6FB71290.comment:
Copies 15-byte network validation data structure to stack and calls FUN_6fb23d20.

Classification: Wrapper/Thunk function

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 16 bytes on stack (0x10)
2. Copy bytes 0-3 from input to stack (dwField0)
3. Copy bytes 4-7 from input to stack (dwField4)
4. Copy bytes 8-11 from input to stack (dwField8)
5. Copy bytes 12-13 from input to stack (wFieldC)
6. Copy byte 14 from input to stack (byFieldE)
7. Pass stack buffer address to FUN_6fb23d20
8. Clean up stack and return

Parameters:
pNetValidationData (ECX) - Pointer to NetValidationData structure (15 bytes)

Returns:
void - No return value

Structure Layout (NetValidationData, 15 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field     Type    Description
0x00    4     dwField0  uint    First DWORD of validation data
0x04    4     dwField4  uint    Second DWORD of validation data
0x08    4     dwField8  uint    Third DWORD of validation data
0x0C    2     wFieldC   ushort  WORD field of validation data
0x0E    1     byFieldE  byte    Final byte of validation data

Notes:
No callers found in this module (likely called from external code or via function pointer).
FUN_6fb23d20 is a network validation state handler that processes game state transitions.
The stack copy may be for thread safety or to avoid modifying original data.

0x6FB712D0.name: ProcessInventoryPageWrapper
0x6FB712D0.comment:
Wrapper function that copies page data to a protected stack buffer before processing.

Classification: Thunk/Wrapper - copies data to protected stack then delegates.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 48-byte stack buffer (SUB ESP, 0x30)
2. Save ESI and EDI registers (PUSH ESI, PUSH EDI)
3. Load source pointer from ECX into ESI (MOV ESI, ECX)
4. Set loop counter to 11 DWORDs (MOV ECX, 0xB)
5. Set destination to stack buffer (LEA EDI, [ESP+8])
6. Copy 44 bytes via REP MOVSD (11 iterations x 4 bytes)
7. Copy final byte via MOVSB (byte 45 of 45)
8. Load stack buffer address to ECX for fastcall (LEA ECX, [ESP+8])
9. Call ProcessInventoryPageOperation(ECX) to process copied data
10. Restore registers and return (POP EDI, POP ESI, ADD ESP 0x30, RET)

Parameters:
pPageData - byte* in ECX (__fastcall), pointer to 45-byte page data structure:
  +0x00: Page operation type char ('9' = delete, else insert/replace)
  +0x03: Page index byte (0-7 valid, 0xFF = invalid)
  +0x0B: Target unit ID (dword)
  +0x0F: Item subtype (ushort)
  +0x11: X position (ushort)
  +0x13: Y position (ushort)
  +0x21: Inventory mode flag (dword)

Returns:
void - All operations performed through ProcessInventoryPageOperation.

Purpose:
Copies volatile page data to protected stack memory before processing,
preventing modification during inventory operations. This ensures atomic
processing of inventory page commands by isolating the data from external changes.

Magic Numbers:
0x30 (48) - Stack buffer size in bytes (45 used + 3 alignment)

0x6FB718C0.name: SubmitPlayerActionEvent
0x6FB718C0.comment:

   - Action type from offset 0x18 (ushort)
   - Priority from offset 0x1a (ushort) 
   - Data value combined from offsets 0x1c and calculated length
   - Timestamp from offset 0x1e (ushort)
   - Flags from offset 0x20 (ushort)
5. Call AddPlayerActionToQueue with extracted parameters and calculated string pointers

Parameters:
pActionEventData - Pointer to PlayerActionEvent structure containing action data

Returns:
void - No return value

Offset Size Field Name    Type      Description
0x00   3    padding       byte[3]   Structure alignment padding
0x03   4    nPlayerId     int       Target player identifier
0x07   1    bActionParam  byte      Action-specific parameter value
0x08   16   szPlayerName  byte[16]  Player name buffer (null-terminated)
0x18   2    wActionType   ushort    Type of action to perform  
0x1a   2    wPriority     ushort    Processing priority level
0x1c   2    wDataLow      ushort    Lower 16 bits of action data
0x1e   2    wTimestamp    ushort    Event timestamp value
0x20   2    wFlags        ushort    Action processing flags
0x22   32   szEventName   char[32]  Event name string buffer

0xffffffff (4294967295) - Initial string length counter for REPNE scan

0x6FB74D90.name: ValidateCoordinatesInBounds

9. Verify entity data exists and field at offset +0x28 matches DAT_6fbf21e8

Returns:

Entity types 7 and 12 allow both horizontal and vertical movement

0x6FB74EA0.signature: void AddRenderQueueEntry(uint * pRenderContext, RenderListNode * pListNode, uint * pEntity, uint dwEntityId)
0x6FB74EA0.comment:

3. Check if queue is not full (limit is 3000 entries)
4. Calculate queue entry pointer: base + (index * 5) + 1 (5 uint elements per entry)
5. Initialize queue entry with type 1 (active), entity reference, and null next pointer
6. Call coordinate transform function (Ordinal_10034) with entity ID and output buffer
7. Calculate transformed X coordinate: (transform_x + entity_x_base * 5) * 8
8. Calculate transformed Y coordinate: (transform_y + entity_y_base * 5) * 8
9. Set bit flag in render context using global bit mask at offset 0xc
10. Find end of linked list starting from list node head pointer
11. Append new queue entry to end of linked list

Parameters:
